questions.question: Direction: Identity the appropriate choice in changing the voice of the following sentence. She was knitting a sweater at that time.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Identity the appropriate choice in changing the voice of the following sentence.

She was knitting a sweater at that time.

options.text: A sweater was being knitted by her at that time.
options.html: A sweater was being knitted by her at that time.

options.text: A sweater was being knitted by her at this time.
options.html: A sweater was being knitted by her at this time.

options.text: She knitted a sweater at that time.
options.html: She knitted a sweater at that time.

options.text: A Sweater has been knitted by her at that time.
options.html: A Sweater has been knitted by her at that time.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'A sweater was being knitted by her at that time.'

Key Points

  • The given sentence is in Past Continuous Tense and in Active Voice.
  • The rule for changing a Past Continuous Tense from Active voice to Passive voice or Passive to Active Voice:
  • Interchange the object and subject with each other, i.e. object of the active sentence become the subject of the passive sentence.
  • Structure: 
    • Subject + was/were + v1 + ing + object (Active Voice)
    • Object + was/were + being + V3 + by Subject (Passive Voice) 
  • Example: 
    • Esha was singing a song. (Active Voice)
    • A song was being sung by Esha. (Passive Voice)
  • ​Thus, the correct answer is Option 1.
    ​​​

Correct sentence: A sweater was being knitted by her at that time.
 

Mistake Points

  •  There may be confusion between Options 1 and 2.
  • "This" is changed to "That" in the case of narration (Direct to Indirect Speech) and not in the case of voices.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Winning the championship was a dream come true for the team, but being awarded the MVP trophy was _________
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Winning the championship was a dream come true for the team, but being awarded the MVP trophy was _________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 4)

Key Points

  • The phrase "the icing on the cake" means something that makes a good situation even better. (केक पर आइसिंग)
    • Example: Getting a promotion was great, but getting a bonus was the icing on the cake.
  • "The icing on the cake" refers to an additional benefit or positive aspect that enhances an already good situation. (केक पर आइसिंग)
    • Example: Winning the championship was a dream come true for the team, but being awarded the MVP trophy was the icing on the cake.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • The silver lining (उजाले की किरण): A positive aspect in an otherwise negative situation.
    • Example: Losing the job was tough, but the silver lining was that it pushed him to start his own business.
  • The bird in the bush (झाड़ी में पक्षी): Refers to something that is uncertain or not in hand.
    • Example: He was tempted by the offer, but he knew it was just a bird in the bush.
  • A cold turkey (ठंडा टर्की): To quit something abruptly, especially an addiction.
    • Example: He decided to quit smoking cold turkey.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the capitalised word in the given sentence. Isabel listened with extreme respect to this ADMONITION.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the capitalised word in the given sentence.

Isabel listened with extreme respect to this ADMONITION.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Option 4' i.e. 'Counsel'.
Key Points
  • 'Admonition' is a word in English that signifies a gentle or friendly reproof, or an expression of warning or disapproval.(सलाह)
    • For example: A teacher's note to a student to limit excessive talking in class would be considered an 'admonition'.
  • The word 'Counsel' (which is Option 4) can be used as a synonym for 'admonition'.
  • 'Counsel' involves offering advice or guidance, usually as a solution or course of action. (परामर्श)
    • For example: "The doctor's counsel helped him understand the necessity of a balanced diet for maintaining good health".
Therefore, the correct answer is: 'Counsel'.
Additional Information
  • Option 1: 'Insult' ("अपमान") denotes disrespectful or scornfully abusive remarks or actions. This is not a synonym of 'admonition'.
  • Option 2: 'Prayer' ("प्रार्थना") signifies a solemn request or thanksgiving to God or an object of worship. It differs from the meaning of 'admonition' and hence, is incorrect.
  • Option 3: 'Council' ("परिषद") is a group of people who meet regularly to make decisions or give advice on a particular subject, typically one that they know a lot about or have a personal interest in. It's not a synonym for 'admonition'.

questions.question: Rewrite the given below sentence with the suitable usage of the Phrasal verb. There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to ______ of the contract.

There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to ______ of the contract.

options.text: There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to back up of the contract.

options.text: There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to back in of the contract.
options.html: There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to back in of the contract.

options.text: There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to back to the contract.

options.text: There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to back out of the contract.
options.html: There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to back out of the contract.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4.

Explanation –

  • The blank space is to be filled with phrasal verbs. Let's understand what are phrasal verbs.
  • A Phrasal verb is a phrase (such as take-off or look down on) that combines a verb with a preposition or adverb or both and that functions as a verb whose meaning is different from the combined meanings of the individual words.
  • Let's see an example of the phrasal verb.
  1. I went out of the room for a moment. ​ 
  • Let's find out the phrasal verb suitable for the given sentence.
  • Option 1 is wrong because "Back up means - to support", which is not related to the sentence.
  • Option 2 & option 3 are also wrong because "back in" and "back to" are not phrasal verbs. It doesn't have meaning.
  • The Phrasal verb used in Option 4 is the correct answer because "Back out means - to choose not to do something agreed". It is suitable for the sentence that is related to the contract.

The complete sentence will be - " There is a twenty-day cooling-off period in which the investor can choose to back out of the contract."

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct speech. Father told his children that he didn't wish to see any of them and ordered them to go away and leave him alone for some time. Father said to his children:

Father told his children that he didn't wish to see any of them and ordered them to go away and leave him alone for some time.

Father said to his children:

options.text: "I didn't wish to see any of you. Go away and leave him alone for some time."

options.html: "I don't wish to see any of you. Go away and leave me alone for some time."

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- "I don't wish to see any of you. Go away and leave me alone for some time."

Key Points

  • Let's look at the steps to change the sentence from indirect to direct speech:
    • When the indirect speech is in the assertive form, we follow the steps given below:
    • The pronoun 'he' is replaced by 'I' accordingly. In the same way, the following changes will take place:
      • them- you, him- me.
    • The auxiliary verb 'didn't' is replaced by 'don't' followed by the 1st form of the verb i.e. wish.
    • The latter part of the sentence is an imperative sentence, hence its direct form will be as:
      • V1 + Obejct.
    • At last line up the remaining part.
       

Following these steps, we finally get- Father said to his children, "I don't wish to see any of you. Go away and leave me alone for some time."

questions.question: Direction: The following passage consists of six sentences. The first and the sixth sentences are given. The middle four sentences in each have been removed and jumbled up. These are labeled P, Q, R, and S. You are required to find out the proper sequence of the four sentences and choose the correct order from the options. S1: If you’re a woman in your 20s, you probably think you don’t have to worry about health problems such as strokes and colon cancer yet. S6: Protect yourself from conditions increasingly affecting younger women. P: But according to new research, they could affect you sooner than you think. Q: Recent studies indicate that some disorders associated with older age are affecting younger adults, while others are greatly influenced by what you do in your 20s and 30s. R: “But it’s important to know that these risk factors are largely preventable." S: “With the epidemic of obesity and sedentary lifestyles, we’re seeing a rise in risk factors like high cholesterol, smoking, and high blood pressure in younger adults,” says Erin Michos, M.D., M.H.S.
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: The following passage consists of six sentences. The first and the sixth sentences are given. The middle four sentences in each have been removed and jumbled up. These are labeled P, Q, R, and S. You are required to find out the proper sequence of the four sentences and choose the correct order from the options.

S1: If you’re a woman in your 20s, you probably think you don’t have to worry about health problems such as strokes and colon cancer yet.

S6: Protect yourself from conditions increasingly affecting younger women.

P: But according to new research, they could affect you sooner than you think. 

Q: Recent studies indicate that some disorders associated with older age are affecting younger adults, while others are greatly influenced by what you do in your 20s and 30s.

R: “But it’s important to know that these risk factors are largely preventable."

S: “With the epidemic of obesity and sedentary lifestyles, we’re seeing a rise in risk factors like high cholesterol, smoking, and high blood pressure in younger adults,” says Erin Michos, M.D., M.H.S.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'PQSR.'

Key Points 

  • While arranging the parts of the passage given in options, we have to find some grammatical or contextual connections between them, so let’s find out.  
    • The first statement in the sequence should be the one that best connects with S1.
    • It should be a continuation or extension of S1.
    • P follows S1 because it is talking about the new research which is connected to Q.
    • Q follows P because it is talking about recent studies that indicate that some disorders are associated with older age.
    • S follows Q because it is talking about the epidemic of obesity and sedentary lifestyles explained by Erin Michos.
    • R follows S because it is directly connected to S6.
    • S6 provides a conclusion to the story.
  • Therefore, the sequence is 'S1PQSRS6.'
  • Thus, the correct answer is 'PQSR.'
  • ​​The correct sequence:

S1- If you’re a woman in your 20s, you probably think you don’t have to worry about health problems such as strokes and colon cancer yet.

P- But according to new research, they could affect you sooner than you think. 

Q- Recent studies indicate that some disorders associated with older age are affecting younger adults, while others are greatly influenced by what you do in your 20s and 30s.

S- “With the epidemic of obesity and sedentary lifestyles, we’re seeing a rise in risk factors like high cholesterol, smoking and high blood pressure in younger adults,” says Erin Michos, M.D., M.H.S.

R- “But it’s important to know that these risk factors are largely preventable."

S6- Protect yourself from conditions increasingly affecting younger women.

Additional Information 

  • Steps for solving Para Jumbles:
    • Clues include pronouns, like he, she, it, this, that, these, those; adverbs like formally, really; article a, an and the; definers like actually, finally, another; connectors like but, yet, both, also and neither nor, or, however, nevertheless.
    • Now, with the help of clues, try to find out qualifier and qualified sentences, so that we can make pairs of qualified and qualifier sentences to eliminate the wrong choices given in the question.
    • After making pairs, start eliminating the wrong choices or options given in the question.
    • In case there is more than one choice, try to follow the sequence of sentences according to the occurrence of the events.

Hinglish 

  • विकल्पों में दिए गए गद्यांश के भागों को व्यवस्थित करते समय, हमें उनके बीच कुछ व्याकरणिक या प्रासंगिक संबंध खोजने होंगे, तो आइए जानें।
    • अनुक्रम में पहला कथन वह होना चाहिए जो S1 के साथ सर्वोत्तम रूप से जुड़ता हो।
    • यह S1 की निरंतरता या विस्तार होना चाहिए।
    • P, S1 का अनुसरण करता है क्योंकि यह new research  के बारे में बात कर रहा है जो Q से जुड़ा है।
    • Q, P का अनुसरण करता है क्योंकि यह recent studies में बात कर रहा है जो दर्शाता है कि older age disorder से जुड़े हैं।
    • S, Q का अनुसरण करता है क्योंकि यह Erin Michos द्वारा समझाया गया मोटापा और गतिहीन जीवन शैली की महामारी के बारे में बात कर रहा है।
    • R, S का अनुसरण करता है क्योंकि यह सीधे S6 से जुड़ा है।
    • S6 कहानी को एक निष्कर्ष प्रदान करता है।
  • इसलिए, अनुक्रम 'S1PQSRS6' है।

questions.question: Fill in the blank with suitable alternative to make it a meaningful sentence: Deva is an amazing dancer. He ______ since his childhood.
questions.questionHtml:
Fill in the blank with suitable alternative to make it a meaningful sentence:
Deva is an amazing dancer. He ______ since his childhood.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'has been performing'.
 
Key Points
  • The verb phrase "has been performing" is in the present perfect continuous tense, which is used to describe an action that started in the past and is still ongoing or relevant.
  • In this sentence, "since his childhood" indicates an action that began in the past and continues up to the present, making present perfect continuous tense appropriate.
  • Option 2 ("have been performing") is incorrect because "Deva" is a singular subject, requiring "has" instead of "have."
  • Option 3 ("had performed") is incorrect because the past perfect tense is used for actions completed before another past action, which is not the case here.
  • Option 4 ("has performed") is incorrect because it doesn’t convey the ongoing nature of the action.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Complete Sentence: "Deva is an amazing dancer. He has been performing since his childhood."
 
Additional Information
  • Option 2: "have been performing" is incorrect because "have" does not match the singular subject "Deva."
  • Option 3: "had performed" is incorrect because past perfect tense is not suitable for describing an ongoing or present-relevant action.
  • Option 4: "has performed" is incorrect because it doesn’t indicate continuity of action.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to change the sentence from direct speech to indirect speech " I have been walking along the river", he said. He said that he ________ along the river.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to change the sentence from direct speech to indirect speech " I have been walking along the river", he said. He said that he ________ along the river.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Had been walking'.
 
Key Points
  • In the given sentence, "I have been walking along the river", he said. Backshifting requires changing the present perfect continuous tense ('have been walking') to the past perfect continuous tense ('had been walking').
  • Consequently, it should be "He said that he had been walking along the river" in indirect speech.
  • This structure (subject + had + been + verb-ing) allows the listener to understand that the action was still going on at the time the person spoke.
Therefore, the correct answer is- ‘Option 1’.
 
Additional Information
  • 'Should be walking' changes the meaning of the sentence, suggesting an obligation or advice instead of stating what was happening.
  • 'Has to walk' also introduces an obligation or necessity, which is not implied in the original sentence.
  • 'Have to walk' is grammatically incorrect. This option changes the sentence from a statement of a happening to one of an obligation. Furthermore, when using indirect speech with said, a past tense is typically required, which this option does not fulfill.

    • "Beside" is incorrect because it refers to being next to something, which does not make sense in this context.
    • Verb Agreement Error in (iii): "rankings has come to dominate" is incorrect because "rankings" is a plural noun and therefore requires the plural form of the verb, "have," making it "rankings have come to dominate."
    • Verb agreement errors occur when the verb does not correctly match the singular or plural status of the subject noun.
  • The correct sentence is: "Since the first appearance of global university ranking systems around two decades ago, rankings have come to dominate the attention in higher education ecosystems around the world."
  • Based on the correct sentence:
    • (i) Since the first appearance of,
    • (iv) higher education ecosystems around the world are the grammatically correct parts.
  • Given this correction, the accurate portrayal of grammatically intact parts are (i) and (iv), because:
    • Part (i) correctly sets up the time frame starting from a historical point without any grammatical issues.
    • Part (iv) correctly discusses the influence of rankings in higher education without any grammatical errors.
  • Therefore, the correct combination of grammatically correct parts, based on the corrected sentence provided and the identified errors, is: (i) and (iv)

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 1 i.e. philosopher.

Key Points

  • The word "philosopher" refers to someone who loves wisdom and pursues knowledge, often in the realm of fundamental nature of reality, existence, and knowledge. (दार्शनिक)
    • Example: Socrates is considered one of the greatest philosophers of all time.
  • "Sycophant" refers to a person who acts obsequiously toward someone important in order to gain advantage; a flatterer. (चापलूस)
    • Example: The sycophant always praised the boss excessively to get promotions.
  • "Philanthropist" means a person who seeks to promote the welfare of others, typically through generous donations of money to good causes. (परमार्थी)
    • Example: The philanthropist donated millions to the charity supporting underprivileged children.
  • "Patriot" refers to a person who vigorously supports their country and is prepared to defend it against enemies or detractors. (देशभक्त)
    • Example: The patriot was willing to sacrifice everything for the love of his country.

Therefore, the correct answer is: philosopher.
